title: Architecture decision record (ADR)
when: The team made or must make a significant technical choice and the user wants it documented with context and tradeoffs.
prompt:
Goal: A short, dated record that explains the context, the options, the decision and its consequences so future readers know why.
Steps:
1. File name docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md with the next number; title # NNNN. Decision in a few words.
2. Status line: Proposed, Accepted, Deprecated or Superseded by NNNN, plus the date.
3. ## Context: the forces at play, constraints and the problem, without arguing for an option yet.
4. ## Options: each with two or three pros and cons in the same format.
5. ## Decision: the chosen option in active voice ("We will store data as JSON files per user").
6. ## Consequences: what becomes easier, what becomes harder, follow up work, and when to revisit.
Quality bar:
- Under one page.
- Options are described fairly.
- Consequences include the downsides.
Pitfalls:
- Writing it after the fact as a justification only.
- Editing an accepted ADR instead of superseding it.
- Mixing several decisions in one record.
Verify:
- [ ] Starts with a # heading with the number.
- [ ] Has Context, Decision and Consequences sections.
- [ ] Status and date are present.
- [ ] Code fences, if any, are closed.
Output: docs/adr/NNNN-title.md and an index line in docs/adr/README.md if one exists.

examples.input: documente por que escolhemos arquivos JSON em vez de banco de dados
examples.output: # 0003. Store data in JSON files, context, 3 options, decision, consequences
